# Results — Study 194 (Turkey) on real ^GSPC tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Signal: the daily
close-to-close log-return of the S&P 500 (^GSPC) on the Wednesday before
Thanksgiving and the Friday after (Black Friday), tested against matched-weekday
baselines. As-of **2026-06-15**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | n trading days | Wed-before-Thanksgiving | Black Fridays | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| ^GSPC (shared cache) | 1928-01-03 → 2026-06-12 | 24,728 | 98 | 97 | `df3897aef897` |

## Primary A — Wednesday before Thanksgiving vs other Wednesdays

| Group | n | mean return (bps/day) | HAC t-stat | Welch p |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Wed before Thanksgiving** | 98 | **+5.87** | +0.46 | — |
| All other Wednesdays | 4,943 | +7.17 | — | — |
| **Contrast (Wed minus other)** | — | **−1.30** | — | **0.9082** |

- The Wednesday-before-Thanksgiving mean is **+5.87 bps/day** vs +7.17 bps for
  other Wednesdays — a contrast of **−1.30 bps** (wrong direction).
- Welch p = **0.91**, HAC t = +0.46. Completely indistinguishable from noise.
- Bonferroni-corrected p (k=2) = **1.00**.

## Primary B — Black Friday (day after Thanksgiving) vs other Fridays

| Group | n | mean return (bps/day) | HAC t-stat | Welch p |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Black Friday** | 97 | **+20.62** | +2.01 | — |
| All other Fridays | 4,847 | +4.36 | — | — |
| **Contrast (Black Fri minus other)** | — | **+16.26** | — | **0.1021** |

- Black Friday mean is **+20.62 bps/day** vs +4.36 bps for other Fridays — a
  contrast of **+16.26 bps**.
- HAC t = **+2.01** (on the Black Friday group in isolation) but Welch two-sample
  t = +1.65 with p = **0.10**. After Bonferroni correction (k=2) p = **0.20**.
- With n=97 events and daily vol ~100 bps, the power to detect a 16 bps effect is
  low; the HAC t barely clears 2 on the group alone but the two-sample test does
  not.

## Placebo — Tuesday before Thanksgiving vs other Tuesdays

| Group | n | mean return (bps/day) | Contrast | p-value |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Tuesday before Thanksgiving** | 98 | **+5.53** | **+1.67 bps** | **0.8751** |

The Tuesday before Thanksgiving (matched window, one day earlier) shows no anomaly
(+1.67 bps contrast, p = 0.88). It does not replicate the Black Friday pattern,
consistent with the effect being concentrated specifically on the half-day after
Thanksgiving rather than general late-November seasonality.

## Multiple-comparisons correction

Two primary hypotheses tested (Wednesday-before, Friday-after); Bonferroni k=2:

| Test | Raw p | Bonferroni p (k=2) | Significant at α=0.05? |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| Wednesday before Thanksgiving | 0.9082 | 1.0000 | No |
| Black Friday (Friday after) | 0.1021 | 0.2042 | No |

Neither test survives the Bonferroni correction. Even the borderline Black Friday
result (raw p = 0.10) is far from the corrected threshold of 0.025.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** Black Friday shows a raw contrast of +16.26 bps and HAC t =
  2.01 (on the group in isolation), but the Welch two-sample p = 0.10 and
  Bonferroni-corrected p = 0.20 both fall short of the inference bar (|t| ≥ 2 on
  the real tape AND survival of multiple-comparisons correction). The Wednesday-before
  effect is absent (contrast −1.30 bps, p = 0.91). With only 97–98 events over 99
  years the study is genuinely underpowered; the Black Friday pattern may be real but
  cannot be certified with the available data.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Even if the Black Friday effect were confirmed, with ~1
  event/year the strategy accumulates return at a rate of ~16 bps/yr. Any realistic
  execution cost (even 5 bps round-trip) would consume a meaningful share of the
  premium, and the uncertainty on the 16 bps estimate is enormous (CI ±~20 bps).
- **Pre-holiday bias** — The Wednesday-before result is a clear null: the most
  canonical "pre-holiday optimism" day at Thanksgiving has no positive edge on the
  S&P 500 over 99 years.
